commits.summary: Bind local manifest lookups to public proofs (verification pending)
commits.body:
Eleven of sixteen disclosed release pairs qualified both finite questions on the original application verifier. The remaining five reached the correct production methods but declared local manifest JARs that were absent. Bind those negative lookups to the selected launch and cache, defer cache writes until they are rechecked, and keep additional or reordered providers open. A signed declaration may revisit an already bound JAR or the immediate next explicit provider. Batik now qualifies all eight entries in its two-width gradient claim in a capped probe. All 49 affected test groups and the test inventory passed.

Recheck cold, warm, clean and wrong expectations on the six original XML and manifest-bearing release pairs. Also insert a real resource at a formerly missing path, explicitly bind it, and restore the original graph. commits.summary: Discover public resource lookup workflows (verification pending)
commits.body:
Give the generator two ordered release graphs and a JDK. It finds public methods that enumerate class-loader resources, derives the marker-specific keys from both original releases, registers line, type and duplicate expectations, and builds independent resource roots and controls. An isolated 16-packet pass found the previously unreachable annotation-index primary and a separate Batik service iterator. All 60 populated original JVM trials matched. The scoped method stops are recorded for the other fourteen projects. All 58 affected groups, compiling all four original comparator adapters, the inventory and job schema passed.

Six original application plans now agree cold, warm and clean and reject the wrong primary. Together the 16 pairs establish all 32 registered finite observations at the declared sample bounds. The manifest appearance control went from 0 to 82, refused an unbound provider and refuted preservation once explicitly bound. An audit checked 72 collected file digests, 40 plans and the registered source. The successor selector and JDK are pinned. The displaced-candidate fallback was independently qualified in a neutral namespace.

commits.summary: Isolate native resource proofs and JVM replays (verification pending)
commits.body:
The previous checker proved a false equivalence for resource bytes 65 and 66. On an independently registered compensating reader it also reported and confirmed a false JVM counterexample of 66 versus 65 although both originals returned 65. Strict native now keeps release-owned loader identities, resolves nested keys on the ordered original graphs, binds virtual resource lookups into the cache, and replays public static integral differences on separate unmodified JVMs. An arbitrary paired-postcondition witness without an original replay remains open. The two original errors, bytecode, classes, JARs and ordinary JVM values are retained.

The corrected ordinary witness returned 65 and 66 and the compensating equality verified. The indexer transfer gave 112 and 113 and the public index consumer observed the expected class names. The JDK 21 cache regression accepted an unchanged hit and rejected an old proof after a same-path JAR changed. All 56 affected groups passed. Both selected JDK 21 regressions passed after correcting an obsolete nested-reflection expectation that the pre-repair binary already proved. The earlier finite measurement audit checked 204 collector outputs, 40 public plans, 68 original automatic or calibration candidates and all 16 full matched references.

The separate prospective pool comprises 85 pairs in 48 new projects. Keep the seed and private screening journal. Thirteen of 18 candidates had a common executable public API and all 26 corresponding signed JARs were verified. No fresh question has been scored. Also check lowercase manifest lookup and both original context-loader return orders. Job 20261124-235933-verify-alternate-manifest-spelling-on-re.
